story: Predicting the next high-frequency function word or comma (the, and, is, to, ',') that continues guidebook prose right after a noun phrase or clause boundary.
Predicting digits in listing metadata - phone numbers after the % marker, prices after '-' or '/', and numbered map-index entries.
Predicting an article ('the', 'a', 'The') that opens a new noun phrase right after a comma, 'and', 'includes', or similar list/clause connective.
Predicting the comma (or small function word) that closes off a long descriptive or appositive noun phrase in mid-sentence guidebook prose.
Predicting the semicolon field separator after a URL, postcode, or opening-hours value in Lonely-Planet-style listing boilerplate (with some spillover onto superlatives after "world's"/"country's").
Predicting the specific content word that completes a hyphenated compound or descriptive phrase seen for the first time ('low-lying', 'palm-tree-lined', 'top end', 'French Gothic').
Re-predicting a proper place name (London, Canterbury, Dover, Greenwich, Camden...) that already appeared earlier in the passage.
Completing split-up words and web addresses - most sharply the 'uk' after '.co.' / '.ac.' in URLs, plus tails of rare words like 'refuelling' and 'omelettes'.
Continuing enumerations and schedule strings with the next separator or item - the final 'and' before the last list item, the range dash or comma inside opening-hours and price sequences.
Ending a completed sentence or listing line - predicting the sentence-final period, or the newline that follows a closing parenthesis or full stop.
Predicting 'com' to finish a web address of the form www.something.[com].

Predicting the next boilerplate symbol in the guidebook listing template - the '%' before a phone number, 'h' before hours, 't' before a tube stop, or the ')' / ';' that closes a (MAP GOOGLE MAP) field - late in a context full of identical listings.
Predicting the main verb (are/is/has) or next continuation right after the subject noun phrase of a sentence ('the cakes and snacks are', 'this old coaching inn has').
Predicting the period (or clause-final comma) that ends a long descriptive sentence whose last word is a content noun ('...shops and eateries.', '...street entertainers and buskers.').
Completing weekday ranges in opening-hours strings - overwhelmingly 'Sat' after 'Mon-' - plus adjacent hours/price field separators.
Predicting the newline that ends a paragraph immediately after a sentence-final period (very high induction - the pattern '.\n' has occurred many times before in the context).
Completing multi-token proper names and abbreviations at their first mention early in the window ('Sloane S->q', 'Motcomb -> St', 'St Katharine D->ocks').
